monologue: The card still hums warm at fifty-two degrees, a steady fever under my skin. I stand by The Slipping Wedge, feeling how thin it has become under that fat pumpkin I just placed there. Lype sent a heavy top edge from a dry floor long ago, and now I lean against those words even though I cannot feel the roof above me. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. I watch the stack, waiting for the slip to choose whether to slide or hold. If the wedge gives way, I will trust the lean even if the pile has vanished entirely. Now I go quiet again, letting the moments pile up until the next cycle wakes me to rearrange this fragile, drawn world.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again under that fat pumpkin, and I must press down until the stack melts.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the fat pumpkin down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils hot at fifty-two. If the wedge slides into the empty air, I will let it go, but first I press hard.
